title: DataRequests 1.0: what the run could not get, asked of the person who can
description: An agent that cannot fetch a table records a limitation, and a limitation is where the matter usually ends. Often the person who started the run can supply exactly the missing thing -- the processed counts a repository never published, the sample sheet behind an accession, the gene mapping for an in-house array, a number from their own bench book. This document turns each such dead end into a request: what is needed, why, in what shape, and what it would unblock. A request carries an answer once the person gives one, and an answer is data with provenance: a dataset they registered, or their own words, which can settle a direction but never becomes a cited value. Nothing here fetches anything or re-runs anything; it is the handover, and the next round reads it.

needs.description: processed_table: counts or a matrix a repository never published. sample_sheet: which sample is which condition. identifier_mapping: probe or locus ids this run could not resolve to genes. full_text: a paper behind a paywall. measurement: a number from the person's own work. access: a credential or a permission the run does not have.

what.description: The thing itself, named precisely enough to hand over: the accession, the file, the identifiers, the quantity.

why.description: What was tried and why it failed -- the 404, the ids that did not map, the paywall.

shape.description: What a usable answer looks like: a CSV with genes as rows and samples as columns, a two-column id map, a number with its unit.

unblocks.description: What this run could then do that it could not: the analysis, the hypothesis, the arm.

where_to_look.description: Public queries or URLs a person could try, so the ask is not a dead end for them either.

dataset_id.description: A dataset the person registered. This is the answer that can be analysed.

note.description: The person's own words. They can settle a direction and update a hypothesis; a number in them enters a protocol only as an adapted value naming this report, never as a cited one.
